claims.text: A 133-character nested ternary expression combined with a complex elsif condition makes the same-organization decision logic hard to read and verify.

The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
The untrusted_attributes list in the serializer spec was not updated to include website_name, so there is no regression test guarding the field-masking bug.
The `include_website_name` method needs to apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` guard as `website`, otherwise the derived URL label can bypass the existing hidden-profile-field check

The `website_name` attribute is not included in `untrusted_attributes`, so it remains visible to anonymous users viewing TL0 profiles even though `website` is correctly hidden, leaking website information that should be restricted
website_name re-parses the same URI up to twice and re-splits the host by '.' up to six times within a single call, which is redundant computation.
There is no test asserting that website_name is absent from the payload when the user hasn't set a website.
URI parsed up to three times per call - URI(website.to_s) is called multiple times to get host and path, should parse once and cache the result
Is the asymmetry in the reverse case (website is a subdomain of the instance domain) intentional, i.e. should the same-domain-family check be bidirectional?

The rescue modifier on URI parsing (`rescue nil`) catches all StandardError, not just URI::InvalidURIError, so a website value containing a space silently makes website_name return nil and hides the entire website UI element (a behavioral regression from the previous frontend implementation).
There is no test covering the elsif branch that the code comment itself describes (www.example.com vs forum.example.com), which is the most logically complex part of the new method.

Can Discourse.current_hostname ever include a port (e.g. localhost:3000)? If so, all comparisons would fall into the 'different domain' branch on non-standard-port deployments since URI#host never includes a port.
Empty string website_host not guarded - URI.host can return empty string for file:/// or data: URIs, and the nil check won't catch this, causing unnecessary serialization of empty website_name

The new website_name serializer attribute is not added to untrusted_attributes, so it bypasses the existing rule that hides fields like website from anonymous viewers of a TL0 user's profile, defeating an existing anti-spam protection.

In website_name, the logic doesn't cover the case where the instance host is the apex domain (e.g. example.com) but the user website is a subdomain (e.g. www.example.com/user); in that case this branch returns only www.example.com without the path. Subdomains of the instance domain may need to include the path as well.

The 'same organization' heuristic (equal label count plus matching domain after dropping the first label) misjudges two-level public suffixes like com.br or co.uk as the same organization, causing an unrelated external domain to be shown with its full path.
Sibling-subdomain case (Case 2 elsif branch) is untested - the branch handling hosts with same number of segments and more than two has no spec coverage
